toc.text: UC3 — Channel Sales with Advanced Approvals

html:
The thirty-one exercises and ten mini projects in this academy are no different from the work a CPQ & Revenue Cloud consultant does in production. This guide turns that toolkit into three complete, end-to-end business scenarios — the kind of engagement that starts as a discovery workshop and ends as a signed-off quote-to-cash implementation.

Each use case below is written the way a consultant brief is written: business background first, then the people involved, the pain they feel today, the requirements the platform must meet, a data-model sketch, and the success metrics the customer will be measured against. The solutions — full object builds, Apex, SOQL, rollout and testing plans — are in Phase 17 and referenced from each case.

The three cases were deliberately chosen to cover the whole academy syllabus:

  • UC1 — Enterprise SaaS Quote-to-Cash exercises the subscription motion: catalog, bundles, pricing rules, approvals, contracts, renewals, billing and revenue recognition. It leans on the SaaS-shaped custom model (Revenue_Schedule__c, Renewal_Opportunity__c, ARR fields on every record).
  • UC2 — Manufacturing Revenue Recognition is the complex-terms motion: bundled machines, milestone and percentage-of-completion recognition, multi-method schedules, and reconciliation against Account.Current_ARR__c.
  • UC3 — Channel Sales with Advanced Approvals is the people and process motion: partner pricing, approval matrices and chains, platform events to an external ERP, and fulfillment tracking. It is where Approval_Log__c, Discount_Schedule__c and Revenue_Sync__e come into their own.

All three use the academy's objects and services exactly as defined in this roadmap — no invented fields, no invented URLs. API version 68.0 throughout.

UC1 — Enterprise SaaS Quote-to-Cash

Business background

VantageGrid provides cloud-based grid-computing and analytics software sold as annual subscriptions. Customers subscribe per compute-seat per month, choose a tier (Pro, Scale, or Enterprise with custom terms), and can add storage and support options. Since the sales team bypassed the deal process ("we shipped customers via spreadsheet"), finance cannot forecast ARR, and two reps have quoted different prices to the same customer in the same week.

The business wants a single motion: quote -> approval -> contract -> billing schedule -> revenue recognition -> renewal forecast, all in Salesforce.

Stakeholders

StakeholderInterest
VP SalesConsistent quoting, fast turn-around, approval SLAs
Enterprise AE / Sales OpsSelf-serve bundling, quote templates, no manual math
Finance ControllerARR forecast, discount discipline, audit trail
Renewals teamNext renewal date and uplift for every contract
Revenue accountingStraight-line recognition that matches billing

Current pain

  • Quotes built in spreadsheets: no configuration validation, prices drift between reps.
  • No enforced discount threshold — a 40% discount and a 4% discount go through the same path with no approver.
  • No contract record until the legal doc; renewal dates are re-derived by hand every quarter.
  • "Revenue" is a lump sum on the invoice; accounting re-splits it monthly in a separate workbook.

Requirements

#Requirement
R1Quote seat-based subscriptions from one catalog with bundles and option constraints
R2Pricing driven by a volume Discount_Schedule__c + price-rule engine
R3Automatic approval routing: up to 10% rep-auth, 10-25% manager, above 25% executive
R4One won quote generates one Draft contract carrying ARR, term and auto-renew flag
R5Near-expiry contracts generate Renewal_Opportunity__c predictions with uplift
R6Orders create monthly Revenue_Schedule__c rows that sum exactly to annual ARR
R7Scheduled recognition flips matured rows to Recognized and rolls ARR to the account
R8Every approval hop and sync event is logged for audit (Approval_Log__c, Revenue_Sync__e)

Data model sketch

text
Account ─< Opportunity ─< Quote ─< QuoteLineItem (parent/options, discounts)
                             1│
                             1│  Contract ─< Renewal_Opportunity__c
                               Order ─< Revenue_Schedule__c (Quote/Contract/Order/Account)
Account.Current_ARR__c  = SUM(Revenue_Schedule__c.Recognized_Amount__c)
Quote.Total_ARR__c      = SUM(QuoteLineItem.Net_Unit_Price__c * Quantity)
Approval_Log__c         = every routing/decision hop on the quote

Success metrics

MetricTarget
Quote turnaround (proposal -> approval)Under 24h for standard deals
Discount leakage (list vs net)Under 8% blended
Contracts from won quotes100% automated, no manual record
Renewal coverage100% of contracts have an Open renewal prediction 90 days out
Recognition accuracyScheduled amounts tie to billing to the cent
Audit trail100% of above-threshold discounts have an Approval_Log__c decision

See Phase 17 — ## UC1 Solution for the full build, Apex, and rollout plan.

UC2 — Manufacturing Revenue Recognition

Business background

Meridian Industrial sells heavy equipment (packaging lines, compressors) plus long-term service maintenance agreements (M&S). A "deal" is a bundle: the machine, a commissioning fee, spare kits, and a 36-month maintenance plan. Payment is milestone-based (30% at PO, 40% at shipment, 30% at acceptance), but revenue must be recognized per ASC 606 / IFRS 15 — some elements at a point in time, others over the term.

Meridian's finance team currently re-recognizes every contract by hand each month-end. Monthly close takes six days, and the auditors ask for evidence of timing and method for every revenue line.

Stakeholders

StakeholderInterest
Director of SalesBundled equipment + M&S priced consistently in one quote
Legal / ContractsTerms, milestones and acceptance dates on the contract record
Revenue accounting leadASC 606 / IFRS 15 recognition method per performance obligation
Order managementFulfillment milestones (shipped/delivered/commissioning) drive billing
CFO / ControllerRecognition timing tied to delivery events, not invoice lags

Current pain

  • Bundles are BOMs in a spreadsheet: 5% of quotes have option conflicts that surface at manufacturing.
  • One recognition method applied to everything, so service revenue is recognized too early.
  • Milestones exist in email, not in the platform — recognition is back-dated and error-prone.
  • Month-end requires six manual days; auditors request schedules that do not exist in the system.

Requirements

#Requirement
R1Bundle machine + commissioning + spare kits + M&S plan with single-select groups
R2Quarterly/point-in-time vs over-time recognition expressed as Recognition_Method__c per schedule row
R3Milestone billing produces schedule rows keyed to fulfillment dates, not invoice uploads
R4Recognition service tolerates partial periods (recognized amount on a date, not just binary)
R5Account roll-up and dashboards reconcile recognized revenue to monthly close
R6Audit view: every recognized row shows Status__c, method, date and amount

Data model sketch

text
Quote ─ QuoteLineItem (bundle parent + option lines w/ Bundle_Option__c)
Contract ─< Order ─< Revenue_Schedule__c
    Recognition_Method__c : 'Straight Line' | 'At Point in Time' | 'Percentage of Completion'
    Status__c : Pending -> Recognized
Account <────────── Current_ARR__c (roll-up of recognized amounts)
Approval_Log__c      (large M&S discounts route like UC1/UC3)

Success metrics

MetricTarget
Month-end close durationFrom 6 days to under 3
Recognition method coverage100% of contract revenue rows carry a method
Bundle defect rateOptions validated before manufacturing: zero conflicts
Audit evidence100% of recognized rows have dated, method-labeled records
Remeasurement speedRe-running recognition for a date returns identical rows

See Phase 17 — ## UC2 Solution for the full build, Apex, and rollout plan.

UC3 — Channel Sales with Advanced Approvals

Business background

Northwind Partners is a manufacturer of network infrastructure sold through a two-tier channel: distributors and resellers. Reps quote via partners (Gold, Silver, Bronze tiers), margins differ by tier, and discounts beyond partner authority must escalate through a chain: partner manager -> channel director -> executive for anything above 25%, large strategic deals, or any deal in certain regions.

The approval path today is email ping-pong. Partners re-quote because they never learn the decision, sales ops replays status across three spreadsheets, and the ERP (legacy order system) is fed by manual re-entry — with order numbers re-keyed by hand.

Stakeholders

StakeholderInterest
Channel AEsPartner-facing quotes with tier-based pricing and margin visibility
Channel operationsA single approval matrix instead of email chains
Distributors / resellersKnow their deal status without asking again
FinanceDiscount and margin leakage visible per partner tier
Sales ops / ITQuote-to-ERP sync with order numbers returned to the quote

Current pain

  • Approver lookup is tribal knowledge; two regions route the same discount differently.
  • No audit trail: channel disputes "who approved what" monthly.
  • Tier pricing is a static table in a deck; price exceptions balloon out of control.
  • ERP order numbers are keyed in by hand after the deal closes — order mismatches weekly.

Requirements

#Requirement
R1Partner tier governs list price exposure and baseline margin (Account.Partner_Tier__c)
R2Approval matrix: authority by discount threshold, region, and strategic flag
R3Approval chains persist every hop as an Approval_Log__c row with date, approver and decision
R4Threshold control enforced by service, not by user discipline (ApprovalRoutingService)
R5On approval, publish Revenue_Sync__e; a subscriber syncs the order to the ERP and stores ERP_Order_Number__c
R6Fulfillment progression tracked (Fulfillment_Status__c) and visible to partner/ops
R7Discount leakage reported by partner tier for quarterly business reviews

Data model sketch

text
Account.Partner_Tier__c: Gold | Silver | Bronze
Quote ── ApprovalRoutingService ──> Approval_Log__c (each hop: type, approver, decision, date)
Quote ─ Approval_Status__c change ─> Revenue_Sync__e (Outbound, ApprovalSync)
    └─ subscriber ─> ERP ─> Order.ERP_Order_Number__c
Order ── OrderFulfillmentService ──> Pending -> Shipped -> Delivered + Fulfillment_Date__c
Discount_Schedule__c: baseline volume tiers per product family

Success metrics

MetricTarget
Approval cycle timeUnder 48h for chain approvals (was email-weeks)
Approval audit100% of >25% discounts logged with approver and date
ERP sync accuracy100% of approved orders carry an ERP order number
Leakage by tier< 10% blended; Bronze vs Gold spread visible in dashboard
Fulfillment visibilityPartners/ops see Pending -> Shipped -> Delivered live

See Phase 17 — ## UC3 Solution for the full build, Apex, and rollout plan.

The next guide — 17 — Use Case Solutions — is the implementation reference for all three cases: step-by-step object builds, Apex and SOQL against the academy's ten services, phased rollout, test/validation, and expected outcomes.
